Pozzik, the head goblin engineer out at the Mirage Raceway, needs materials to shave critical ounces off his rocket-car chassis. Rather than relying purely on heavy metal plating, the goblins salvage hollow bones from local desert vultures to build sturdy, ultralight steering and structural rigs.

Across the blinding white expanse of the Shimmering Flats, the rivalry between goblin and gnomish engineers is decided by fractions of a second. Raw engine thrust is useless if a racer is weighed down by excessive bulk. While gnome teams obsess over intricate gears and brass fittings, the goblin crew led by Pozzik seeks ruthless pragmatic efficiency: stripping out dense iron framing and replacing it with lighter, hollow structural components wherever the frame permits.

Rather than shipping expensive, specialized composites out to Thousand Needles, Pozzik turns to the surrounding salt wastes. Salt Flats vultures are plentiful, their skeletons honed by flight to possess hollow, honeycombed cores that provide great tensile strength with almost no mass. By substituting worked vulture bones into the racer's steering rig and minor braces, Pozzik's mechanics aim to keep their machines nimble enough to outmaneuver the gnomes without shaking apart at top speed.

Goblin engineering favors ingenuity and opportunistic materials. Vulture bones are hollow and naturally lightweight, offering an ideal strength-to-weight ratio to reinforce delicate parts like steering rigs without weighing down the racer.

Pilot Longbeard in Ironforge needs a courier to deliver a crate of reinforced siege engine helmets across the sea to Kalimdor. His friends, the Brassbolts brothers, are testing high-speed rocket cars in the Shimmering Flats and urgently need head protection for their accident-prone test drivers.

While stationed among his aerial machinery in Ironforge, the dwarven aviator Pilot Longbeard received an urgent request from the Shimmering Flats in southern Kalimdor. His friends, a pair of inventive gnomes known as the Brassbolts brothers, had taken up residence on the vast salt pans to race experimental machinery. Longbeard is tied down by military and piloting duties, leaving him unable to deliver the supplies himself.

The Brassbolts' rocket car has turned out to be extraordinarily fast—so fast that their test drivers keep wiping out across the salt beds and suffering severe concussions. Longbeard procures a crate of heavy-duty dwarven Siege Engine helmets to protect their craniums. Delivering the crate gives the gnomes the leverage they need to coax reluctant pilots back behind the wheel of their volatile speed machine.

Verner Osgood, the smith in Lakeshire, has depleted his supply of iron patching together equipment for the beleaguered town guard. With no metal left to shoe the local horses, he sends a courier across Elwynn Forest to enlist help from Smith Argus in Goldshire.
A Frontier Strained to the Limit

Lakeshire sits directly in the crosshairs of gnolls, orcs, and murlocs, yet Stormwind offers precious little reinforcement. The local garrison has to fight daily to keep the township from falling, and that relentless combat wears gear down quickly. Verner Osgood spends nearly every waking hour repairing dented breastplates, reshaping dulled swords, and keeping the town guards clad in iron, exhausting his raw materials in the process.

When a frontier settlement runs completely out of iron, even mundane tasks ground to a halt. Without horseshoes, messengers cannot ride swift relays and draft animals cannot haul supplies across the rocky paths of Redridge. Verner must swallow his pride and appeal to the heartland, sending travelers west down the Three Corners road to Goldshire, where Smith Argus still enjoys regular access to the royal realm's deep mineral stores.
